The PR changes active-memory recall summary truncation to use the existing UTF-16-safe SDK slice helper and adds a regression test for emoji-at-boundary summaries.

PR surface: Source +1, Tests +38. Total +39 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. for source-level reproduction: current main uses raw UTF-16 slicing in the active-memory summary path, and the PR body’s negative-control test demonstrates the dangling-surrogate failure. The new review finding is also source-reproducible by comparing old and new truncation behavior for a whitespace-before-emoji boundary.

target.title: fix(active-memory): keep recall summaries UTF-16 safe at truncation boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the active-memory recall summary that gets prepended to the agent prompt could contain a lone UTF-16 surrogate half when the summary was long enough to be truncated and an emoji (or other astral character) sat exactly on the truncation boundary. The broken half renders as a replacement character in the injected `<active_memory_plugin>` context.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateSummary` now cuts with the existing surrogate-safe `sliceUtf16Safe` helper instead of a raw `String.prototype.slice`, so the existing whitespace/word-boundary behavior is preserved while the reserved-ellipsis cut can no longer split a surrogate pair. This mirrors the recently merged tool-summary fix (#98644), which applied the same helper to the same class of user-visible truncation.

## User Impact

Recall summaries containing emoji or other astral Unicode now truncate cleanly at the character before the emoji instead of leaking a broken half-character into the prompt context.

## Evidence

Premise: `String.prototype.slice` operates on UTF-16 code units, so `slice(0, n)` where index `n` falls inside a surrogate pair keeps a dangling high surrogate. `sliceUtf16Safe` (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`) is the existing accepted helper for this exact case and is already used by the merged tool-summary fix (#98644) and by sibling channels (Discord model picker, Feishu streaming card).

Negative control — temporarily restored the raw `trimmed.slice(0, contentMaxChars)` in `extensions/active-memory/index.ts` and ran the new regression test, which drives the real `before_prompt_build` plugin hook (only the embedded recall subagent is mocked). The dangling-surrogate assertion fails, reproducing the leak:

```text
FAIL |extension-active-memory| extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts > truncates recall summaries on a UTF-16 boundary without leaking a lone surrogate
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
- Expected
+ Received
- false
+ true
```

After restoring the fix, the same real-path test passes and the whole file is green:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts -t "UTF-16 boundary"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed | 154 skipped (155)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  155 passed (155)
```

Type-check, format, and lint on the changed files:

```text
pnpm tsgo:extensions            // passed
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test       // passed
pnpm format:check -- extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts   // exit 0
```

What was not tested: no live model round-trip was run to generate a real emoji-bearing recall summary; the regression drives the real plugin hook with a mocked recall subagent, which is sufficient because the truncation happens in-process before the summary is inserted into the prompt, independent of how the summary text was produced.

AI-assisted: implemented with Cursor; all proof commands were run manually.
